tagline: TestForge auditing TestForge. Self-audit shipping fixes for what it finds, in public.

findings.title: OWASP Top 10 analyzer coverage: 80% (8/10)
findings.description: TestForge ships rules for 8 of the 10 OWASP 2021 categories. Categories without dedicated rules yet: A08:2021 — Software and Data Integrity Failures, A10:2021 — Server-Side Request Forgery. These are gaps in the analyzer itself — your project may still have issues in these areas that this report won't surface.
findings.fixSuggestion: For the un-covered categories, complement TestForge with: dependency-track for A08 (software integrity), an SSRF-focused fuzzer or proxy-based runtime scan for A10. Track the gap in your threat model.

findings.title: 59 package(s) installed at multiple versions
findings.description: Version drift inflates bundle size and is a red flag for transitive-dep replacement attacks. Examples: @esbuild/android-arm @ {0.18.20, 0.25.12, 0.27.0, 0.27.2, 0.28.0}; @esbuild/android-arm64 @ {0.18.20, 0.25.12, 0.27.0, 0.27.2, 0.28.0}; @esbuild/android-x64 @ {0.18.20, 0.25.12, 0.27.0, 0.27.2, 0.28.0}.
findings.fixSuggestion: Use `npm ls <name>` to find which deps pin the older version. Add an `overrides` entry to deduplicate, or upgrade the parent dep.

findings.title: License audit could not run — no node_modules/ found
findings.description: License compliance requires reading each installed package's `license` field, but no `node_modules/` directory was present.
findings.fixSuggestion: Run `npm install` (or your package manager's equivalent) before the analysis, or supply pre-installed dependencies. Without this, 62 declared deps are unchecked for license compatibility.

findings.title: Estimated mutation score: ~39% (heuristic)
findings.description: Inputs: 24 test files / 282 source files (ratio 0.09), 749 assertions (601 strong, 132 weak, 3 snapshot), 14 distinct strong-matcher type(s). ~784/2011 candidate mutants likely killed. Run Stryker for the exact number.
findings.fixSuggestion: Boost the kill rate: replace `toBeTruthy()` with `toBe(specificValue)`, add boundary-condition tests, vary the matcher types you use.

findings.title: 1 test file(s) dominated by weak assertions
findings.description: Files where >50% of assertions are toBeTruthy / toBeFalsy / toBeDefined / toBeNull. Examples: mcp-server/tests/fixtures/mutation-quality/tests/weak.test.js (5/5 weak).
findings.fixSuggestion: A mutation that changes `42` to `41` still satisfies `toBeTruthy()`. Replace with `toBe(42)` or `toEqual({…})` to actually catch behaviour changes.

findings.title: 1 test file(s) dominated by snapshot assertions
findings.description: Files where ≥90% of assertions are toMatchSnapshot / toMatchInlineSnapshot. Examples: mcp-server/tests/fixtures/mutation-quality/tests/snapshot.test.js (3/3).
findings.fixSuggestion: Snapshots catch SOME mutants but are brittle (changes in unrelated fields cause failures). Mix in concrete assertions on the values that actually matter.

findings.title: Mutation testing tool not configured
findings.description: Stryker Mutator or similar not found in devDependencies. Install to get real mutation scores.
findings.fixSuggestion: npm install -D @stryker-mutator/core && npx stryker init

findings.title: Potential N+1 Query in for-of
findings.description:
`db.execute()` is invoked inside a `for-of` loop at scripts/seed.js:70. Each iteration issues its own DB round-trip.
Line: await db.execute(sql`
findings.fixSuggestion: Batch the query: pre-build the id list, fire one query with `WHERE id IN (...)`, or use eager-loading (`.include()` / `.populate()` / `JOIN`). For parallelisation only, wrap in `Promise.all([...].map(...))` so the round-trips overlap.

findings.title: 9 Unused Dependencies
findings.description: Dependencies not imported anywhere: @hookform/resolvers, @neondatabase/serverless, @upstash/ratelimit, @upstash/redis, @xyflow/react, …. These increase bundle size, install time, and supply-chain attack surface.
findings.fixSuggestion: Remove with: `npm uninstall @hookform/resolvers @neondatabase/serverless @upstash/ratelimit`. Confirm with `npx depcheck` before removing — some packages are loaded by side-effect (Babel plugins, polyfills) without explicit imports.

findings.title: 441 Exported Symbols Not Referenced Anywhere
findings.description:
Exports that no other file imports:
  api/_session.js: verifySession
  api/_security.js: applySecurityHeaders
  api/_gate.js: monthStartIso, getPlanForUser
  api/_env.js: optionalEnv
  src/lib/api.ts: HealthResponse, checkHealth, Project, getProjects, getProject…
findings.fixSuggestion: Either remove the export, narrow it to `@internal` / non-exported, or use it from another module. For dual-purpose exports (used by external consumers via the package surface), add them to the package's main entry index file so they're reachable.

findings.title: No graceful shutdown handler
findings.description: No `process.on('SIGTERM', …)` or `process.on('SIGINT', …)` listener found. Container orchestrators send SIGTERM before SIGKILL; without a handler, in-flight requests are dropped.
findings.fixSuggestion: Register a SIGTERM listener: `process.on('SIGTERM', async () => { await server.close(); /* drain DB pool, redis, ... */ process.exit(0); });`. Kubernetes sends SIGTERM 30s before SIGKILL.

findings.title: No global error handler registered
findings.description: For Express, no `app.use((err, req, res, next) => …)` 4-arg middleware found. For Fastify, no `setErrorHandler`. Errors propagating to the framework will return generic 500s without structured logging.
findings.fixSuggestion: Express: `app.use((err, req, res, next) => { logger.error(err); res.status(500).json({ error: err.message }); });`. Fastify: `app.setErrorHandler(...)`. Log + return a stable error shape.

findings.title: No `unhandledRejection` / `uncaughtException` guard
findings.description: Node's default behavior on unhandled promise rejection is to crash the process. Without a guard, you can't log the rejection or trigger a graceful drain.
findings.fixSuggestion: `process.on('unhandledRejection', (reason) => { logger.fatal({ reason }, 'unhandled rejection'); process.exit(1); });` — log it, then exit. Letting the process die after logging is fine; silently swallowing the rejection is not.

findings.title: Payment-related code without Idempotency-Key handling
findings.description: Payment / billing dependencies detected, but no read of the `Idempotency-Key` header. Network retries can double-charge customers.
findings.fixSuggestion: Require `Idempotency-Key` on mutating payment endpoints. Cache the result by key + endpoint for ≥24 hours. Stripe's API uses this convention.

findings.title: Small Connection Pool (10) — Will Exhaust Under Agentic Load
findings.description: Your DB connection pool is limited to 10. AI agents making parallel requests will exhaust this quickly — each agent may hold 2-3 connections for chained queries.
findings.fixSuggestion: Increase connection pool to 50+. Use PgBouncer for connection multiplexing. Consider read replicas for agentic workloads.

findings.title: Heavy inline styles in 32 file(s) without CSS Modules
findings.description: 119 inline `style={{…}}` JSX props across 32 files; no CSS Modules detected. Example file: src/pages/Testing.tsx.
findings.fixSuggestion: Adopt CSS Modules / Tailwind / styled-components / vanilla-extract. Inline styles defeat selector caching and make visual-diff testing unstable.

findings.title: 30 hardcoded pixel value(s) in inline styles
findings.description: Pixel values inside JSX `style={{…}}` props. These don't scale to user font-size preferences and break visual-regression snapshots across viewports.
findings.fixSuggestion: Use rem/em or design tokens. Pull from a shared theme so the snapshot baseline can move atomically.

findings.title: 20 inline color literal(s) in JSX styles
findings.description: Hex colors (#abc / #abcdef) embedded directly in `style={{…}}` props. Visual themes can't roll out (dark mode, brand changes) without grepping every file.
findings.fixSuggestion: Pull colors from a theme object (`theme.colors.primary`) or CSS variables.

findings.title: No observability stack detected
findings.description: No APM (OpenTelemetry/Datadog/NewRelic/Honeycomb) and no error tracking (Sentry/Rollbar/Bugsnag) dep detected. Without these, you can't correlate user-impacting issues with code changes.
findings.fixSuggestion: Start with Sentry — fastest path to crash/error visibility. Add OpenTelemetry if you need full tracing. Wire up alerts to a notification channel humans actually read.

findings.title: No feature-flag platform
findings.description: Feature flags decouple deploy from release: kill-switch on regressions, staged rollouts to a % of users, A/B test cohorts. Releases without them are all-or-nothing.
findings.fixSuggestion: For early-stage: Posthog (free tier, JS-SDK-only). For larger teams: LaunchDarkly / Statsig. Even a homegrown flags table beats no kill-switch.

findings.title: No product analytics dependency
findings.description: No Posthog / Mixpanel / Amplitude / Segment / Heap / Plausible / Fathom dep detected. Without telemetry on feature adoption + user journeys, you can't close the loop between code shipped and value delivered.
findings.fixSuggestion: PostHog (open source, generous free tier) is the lowest-friction start. Track 3-5 key events: signup, activation, first-value-moment, retention, churn signal.

findings.title: TypeScript without strict mode
findings.description: tsconfig.json found but `compilerOptions.strict` is not true. The default loose mode lets `any`-typed values flow freely; null/undefined errors slip past the compiler.
findings.fixSuggestion: Set `"strict": true` in tsconfig (turns on strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, strictFunctionTypes, etc.). For an existing codebase, use `tsc --noEmit` to see what breaks, then file by file.

findings.title: No testing framework detected
findings.description: No jest / vitest / mocha / ava / tap dep found. Tests are the #1 predictor of low regression rates.
findings.fixSuggestion: Vitest is the fast modern default (Vite-native, ESM-first). Start with unit tests for the most-edited modules.

findings.title: Large app without monorepo tooling
findings.description: 62 deps without a workspace manager (Turborepo / Nx / pnpm workspaces). Build cache and parallelism are leaving cycles on the table.
findings.fixSuggestion: Turborepo has the lowest adoption cost (drop-in for existing repos). Nx is heavier but ships codegen + generators.

findings.title: CI runs without a type-check step
findings.description: Found 3 CI job(s) but none of them runs `tsc --noEmit` / `type-check`. Type errors only surface at build time or in production.
findings.fixSuggestion: Add a `type-check` step to CI: `run: tsc --noEmit`. Make it a required check on the protected branch.

findings.title: No observability dependency detected
findings.description: No Sentry / Datadog / NewRelic / OpenTelemetry / Honeycomb / Rollbar / Bugsnag dep. MTTR depends on knowing something broke before customers report it.
findings.fixSuggestion: Add error-tracking (Sentry is the easiest) and ideally a tracing stack (OpenTelemetry → Honeycomb / Datadog / Jaeger). Wire up alerts to a notification channel that humans actually read.

findings.title: No CODEOWNERS file detected
findings.description: No `.github/CODEOWNERS` (or `CODEOWNERS` / `docs/CODEOWNERS`). Code reviews route by chance; sensitive areas (auth, billing, infra) lack named approvers.
findings.fixSuggestion: Create `.github/CODEOWNERS` with at minimum: `*.tsx @ui-team`, `src/auth/ @security`, `infra/ @platform`. Make CODEOWNERS-required a branch protection rule.
